legal_chain: Section 8 of the 2002 Act repeals the Forest Renewal Act.

Section 28(1) dissolves Forest Renewal BC and its section 5 committees upon that repeal, rescinds board/committee appointments, vests rights/property/assets in government and makes government liable for obligations.
Section 32 postpones relevant provisions to LGIC regulation.
OIC517/2002 invokes that authority and brings sections 7-11 (including 8) and 28 into force, without specifying a different effective date.
Regulation 158/2002 was deposited 27 June 2002; the Regulations Act default deposit rule fixes that effective date.
forest_renewal.date_14_june_status: Not established as statutory dissolution by the inspected primary instruments. The audit makes no claim about whether it described an operational/administrative milestone.

original_claims.subject: Forest Renewal BC
original_claims.claim: Forest Renewal BC and its statutory committees were dissolved; their assets vested in government and government assumed their liabilities.
original_claims.locator: Budget Measures Implementation Act, 2002 SBC c7: s8 repeals Forest Renewal Act; s28 effects dissolution and vesting. OIC 517 approved 26 June; Reg 158 deposited 27 June.
original_claims.caveat: 14 June is not the statutory dissolution day. The order-making day and commencement day differ.

original_claims.subject: Coastal Ferry Services Contract
original_claims.claim: The first Coastal Ferry Services Contract took effect on 1 April 2003 for a sixty-year term.
original_claims.locator: Original agreement effective-date recital and s3.01; unofficial consolidation effective 1 April 2024, s3.01.
original_claims.caveat: The end date is calculated from the sixty-year term. Four-year performance terms and their amendments are not sixty-year contract renewals. See the separate eighteen-instrument amendment ledger.
